summary: This article explains what the Sun is made of, how fusion in its core makes light and heat, what sunspots and auroras are, and how people use solar energy.
introduce: Write the key term “core” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Our Sun: A Star Up Close” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: the joining of two or more things into one; in stars, tiny particles join and give off energy
the lightest gas; it is the main material that stars are made of

challengeTerms.def: the bright, visible surface layer of the Sun
energy that travels outward as waves or tiny particles, such as light and heat
colorful, glowing lights that sometimes appear in the night sky near the North or South Pole

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the Sun is the most important object in our sky? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the Sun makes its energy and how that energy reaches Earth.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review core, fusion, and hydrogen, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses photosphere, radiation, and aurora to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
